sample.name: Underground Arts
facts: Started as a vision to open the basement of the Wolf Building as a space for free artistic expression.
Occupies 12,000 square feet with two rooms and a 650 capacity club.
Focuses mainly on live music and also hosts theater and fashion shows.

sample.name: Arch Enemy Arts
facts: Accepts Bitcoin
Address: 109 Arch Street, Philadelphia

sample.name: Main Line Art Center
facts: Has served the community for over 75 years as an art school and gallery.
Offers up to ten exhibitions a year, including seasonal fine crafts shows.
Address: 746 Panmure Road

sample.name: Fairmount Water Works Interpretive Center
facts: Run by Philadelphia Parks & Recreation and Philadelphia Water Department
Address: 640 Waterworks Drive, Philadelphia

sample.name: Museum for Art in Wood
facts: Founded in 1986 and formerly called the Center for Art in Wood.
Permanent collection of about 1,200 handmade objects, from everyday items to sculpture.
Address: 141 North 3rd Street, Philadelphia

sample.name: Philadelphia Museum of Jewish Art
facts: Was founded in 1975 and is located within Congregation Rodeph Shalom.
Exhibits contemporary art that illuminates the Jewish experience.
Its permanent collection includes works by Chaim Gross, Tobi Kahn, Joan Snyder and Roman Vishniac.

sample.name: Museum of Illusions Philadelphia
facts: Part of the global Museum of Illusions group.
Has more than 60 exhibits including holograms, stereograms and immersive rooms.
Occupies about 5,000 square feet.

sample.name: Twelve Gates Arts
facts: Founded in 2011 as an arts gallery in Old City.
Highlights South Asian diasporic artistic voices through quarterly visual exhibitions and community events.
Address: 106 North 2nd Street, Philadelphia

sample.name: Philosophical Hall
facts: Built from 1785 to 1789 as the headquarters of the American Philosophical Society.
Is the only privately owned structure on Independence Square.
A loan from society member Benjamin Franklin provided the final money needed to finish construction.

sample.name: Mummers Museum
facts: Address: 1100 South 2nd Street, Philadelphia

sample.name: National Liberty Museum
facts: Founded by publisher Irvin J. Borowsky and his daughter Gwen Borowsky.
Displays the 20-foot glass sculpture Flame of Liberty by Dale Chihuly.
Founded in 2000

sample.name: American Swedish Historical Museum
facts: Opened in 1938
Address: 1900 Pattison Avenue, Philadelphia

sample.name: The Rosenbach Museum & Library
facts: Holds the collections of rare book dealers A. S. W. Rosenbach and his brother Philip H. Rosenbach.
Housed in two 19th-century townhouses at 2008-2010 Delancey Place near Rittenhouse Square.
The Rosenbach brothers lived at 2010 Delancey Place from 1926 to 1952.

sample.name: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts
facts: Is the longest continuously operating art museum and art school in the United States.
Was founded by painter Charles Willson Peale, sculptor William Rush and other artists and business leaders.
The current building was designed by Frank Furness and George Hewitt, begun in 1871 and opened in 1876.

sample.name: Merchants' Exchange Building
facts: Designed by William Strickland
Built in the Greek Revival architecture style
Designated: National Historic Landmark

sample.name: Marvin Samson Center for the History of Pharmacy
facts: Established in 1995 to coincide with the 175th anniversary of the Philadelphia College of Pharmacy.
Holds over 8,000 pharmaceutical and medical artifacts dating back to the 1600s.
Located on the first floor of Griffith Hall on the university's West Philadelphia campus.

sample.name: Penn Museum
facts: First phase completed in 1899 to house finds from the Nippur expedition.
Rotunda with Harrison Auditorium completed in 1915.
Coxe Memorial Wing by Charles Klauder opened in 1926 for the Egyptian collection.
